prerequisites: Calculation and operation skills with simple geometric and algebraic notions
Abilities to use logical thinking and and solve problems

learning_outcomes.text: Explain the fundamental notions of Newtonian Mechanics.
Know, define, and explain notions regarding: kinematic characteristics of motion, kinetic characteristics.
Use vectorial and matrix calculus to interpret the effect of interactions on macroscopic bodies.
Kinematically analyze systems of macroscopic bodies.
Evaluate and describe the type of motion of a material point / a macroscopic body.
Determine moments of inertia for macroscopic bodies that may or may not have an axis of symmetry.
Identify and understand different types of particular motions of rigid bodies, both from a kinematic and dynamic perspective.
Efficiently use available physical and mathematical models in the kinematic and dynamic analysis of motion.
Synthesize relevant aspects in the context of motion.
Solve problems associated with Mechanics and interpret the results.
Critically evaluate and make decisions in accordance with the motion of rigid body systems.
Respect the principles, norms, and values of the professional ethical code by adopting a rigorous, efficient, and responsible work strategy in problem-solving and decision-making.
Select and analyze bibliographic sources specific to the field.
Apply effective relationship and teamwork techniques in multidisciplinary teams, across various hierarchical levels.
Continuously inform and document themselves in their own field of activity by adequately using efficient lifelong learning methods and techniques.
Develop professional projects in the field of engineering.

syllabus_topics: Review. Introduction. Kinematics. Kinematics of absolute motion of a material particle.
Kinematic characteristics: Trajectory. Average velocity. Instantaneous velocity. Radial velocity and transverse velocity.
Average acceleration. Normal acceleration and tangential acceleration. Jerk. Higher-order accelerations. Characterization of motion. Areal velocity.
Kinematics of rigid bodies. Rotation matrix. Parametric equations of motion of a rigid body. Instantaneous angular velocity. Velocity field. Properties of the velocity field. Rototranslation axis.
Acceleration field in rigid body motion. Instantaneous angular acceleration. Properties of the acceleration field. Pole of accelerations.

Dynamics. Dynamics of a material point. Fundamental notions. Principles of classical mechanics. Cauchy model. Classification of forces (active forces, constraint forces, environmental resistance force, damping resistance of elastic elements, inertia forces). Example.
Kinetic characteristics in the dynamics of a material point. Momentum. Angular momentum. Kinetic energy. Momentum theorem. Angular momentum theorem. Forms of the energy theorem.
Equations of rigid body dynamics. Dynamics of particular motions of rigid bodies (translational motion, rotational motion around a fixed axis and physical pendulum, plane-parallel motion).
Calculation of axial moments of inertia of rigid bodies.

Kinematics of a material point. Trajectory. Velocity. Hodograph of velocities. Radial velocity. Transverse velocity. Acceleration. Hodograph of accelerations. Normal acceleration. Tangential acceleration. Jerk. Characterization of motion.
Circular motion of a material particle. Study of material point kinematics in polar coordinates.
Rotational motion around a fixed axis. Matrix calculus.
Kinematics of plane-parallel motion. Instantaneous center of rotation. Fixed centroid. Moving centroid.
Dynamics of a material point (motion on an inclined plane, free pendulum in air).
Dynamics of particular cases of rigid body motions (translational motion, rotational motion of a plate around a fixed axis with environmental resistance).
Occupational safety. Presentation of works and equipment.
Study of the reduction of coplanar force systems.
Experimental study of friction stresses. Experimental study of elastic elements.
Kinematics of a material point (air cushion stand). Kinematics of particular cases of rigid body motions (circular translation, plane-parallel motion).
Methods for experimental determination of axial moments of inertia of rigid bodies.

Dynamics of a material point (motion on an inclined plane, pendulum motion, and free fall in air). Dynamics of particular cases of rigid body motions (translational motion, rotational motion of a plate around a fixed axis with environmental resistance).
Make-up sessions. Situation closing.
teaching_methods: Debates based on Power Point presentations
Direct and indirect exploration of reality (experiments, demonstrations, modeling)

assessment_methods.method: Exam/Verification (includes systematic observation, individual/team assignments, case study report, formative tests, summative test)
Laboratory (includes completion of lab sheets, teamwork, application in practice, evaluation test/colloquium)

assessment_rules: The student must be able to correctly define basic concepts (velocity, acceleration, momentum, angular momentum) and apply fundamental principles of classical mechanics to elementary situations. The final evaluation result for a discipline is obtained by considering the scores and weights assigned to each activity within the discipline. Whole grades from 1 to 10 will be awarded, with a grade of 5 certifying the achievement of the minimum learning outcomes for the discipline and the award of corresponding study credits.
